newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends steady at lower levels after dip.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends steady at lower levels after dip.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures ended steady at the lower levels after dipping in early afternoon trade on expectations that Iraq oil could be flowing to the market by mid-December, traders said.

Within minutes of a Turkish minister saying Iraqi crude was expected to start flowing through the trans-Turkey pipeline by December 15, Jan Brent fell around 25-30 cents a barrel to a low of $22.55. The contract settled at $20.60, down 12 cents.
"Iraqi oil will start flowing by December 15 at the latest through the Kirkuk-Yumurtalik pipeline," Turkish State Minister Lutfi Esengun said after a cabinet meeting in Ankara.

The first Iraqi crude is expected to go to Turkish refineries which have booked oil under the oil-for-food plan. Under the terms of the U.N. oil-for-food deal, Iraq would be allowed to sell $2 billion worth of oil to buy food and medicine.
Traders said cold weather across most of Europe as well as the northeast United States was supportive and continued to underpin prices despite todays fall.

Gas oil futures were also slightly softer at the close with the crude fall erasing some of the early gains made on the back of Wednesday's NYMEX heat expiry strength, but cold weather and talk of arbitrage to the U.S. and Asia provided a brake.
The December gas oil contract last traded $1.25 a tonne firmer at $217.75, 25 cents off ther day's low.
